The '''elongated triangular bipyramid''' or '''elongated triangular dipyramid'''{{sfnp|Francis|2013|loc=See at the line 14}} is a polyhedron constructed from a [[triangular prism]] by attaching two [[regular tetrahedra]] to its bases. It is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s and a [[composite polyhedron]]. This polyhedron is found in the African musical instrument ''nirrosula'' and the [[raphide]] crystal structure in [[plant]]s.

== Construction ==
The elongated triangular bipyramid is constructed from a [[triangular prism]] by attaching two [[regular tetrahedra]] to its triangular bases.{{sfnp|Berman|1971|p=336|loc=See "Table IV: Properties of regular-faced convex polyhedra" at the line 27 in which <math> M_1 </math> is a regular tetrahedron and <math> P_3 </math> is a triangular prism}} Such a process known as [[Elongation (geometry)|''elongation'']].{{sfnp|Berman|1971|p=350}} The triangular prism is [[uniform polyhedron|''uniform'']] (that is, the solid's symmetry maps each vertex to every other vertex), and made of two [[Equilateral triangle|equilateral triangular]] bases and three lateral [[square]] faces. When two regular tetrahedra cover the bases of a prism, the resulting polyhedron has six equilateral triangles and three squares (nine faces in total), fifteen edges, and eight vertices.{{sfnp|Berman|1971|p=336|loc=See "Table IV: Properties of regular-faced convex polyhedra" at the line 27 in which <math> M_1 </math> is a regular tetrahedron and <math> P_3 </math> is a triangular prism}} The elongated triangular bipyramid is a [[Johnson solid]], named after American mathematician [[Norman Johnson (mathematician)|Norman Johnson]] who listed the 92 [[convex polyhedra]] with [[regular polygon]]al faces.{{sfnp|Uehara|2020|p=[https://books.google.com/books?id=51juDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA62 62]}} The elongated triangular bipyramid is enumerated as the fourteenth Johnson solid <math> J_{14} </math>.{{sfnp|Francis|2013|loc=See at the line 14}}{{sfnp|Uehara|2020|p=[https://books.google.com/books?id=51juDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA63 63]}} It is a [[composite polyhedron]], because it can be sliced by a plane to produce convex, regular-faced polyhedra, namely a triangular prism and regular tetrahedra.{{sfnp|Timofeenko|2010|p=484}}

== Properties ==
If the solid's edge-length is <math>a</math>, then its height <math> h </math> is the sum of twice the distance from a vertex to the [[centroid]] of a triangular face in a tetrahedron (<math display="inline"> \sqrt{6}a/3 </math>) and the height of a triangular prism (<math> a </math>):{{sfnp|Özdemir|Özdemir|2021|p=272}}
<math display="block"> h = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}a + \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}a + a = \left(\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3} + 1\right)a \approx 2.633a. </math>
The surface area <math> A </math> of an elongated triangular bipyramid is the sum of the areas of its polygonal faces, which are six equilateral triangles and three squares:{{sfnp|Berman|1971|p=336|loc=See "Table IV: Properties of regular-faced convex polyhedra" at the line 27}}{{sfnp|Özdemir|Özdemir|2021|p=272}}
<math display="block"> A = 6\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2\right) + 3a^2 = \left(\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2} + 3\right)a^2 \approx 5.598a^2. </math>
The volume of an elongated triangular bipyramid is the sum of twice the volume of a tetrahedron and triangular prism:{{sfnp|Berman|1971|p=336|loc=See "Table IV: Properties of regular-faced convex polyhedra" at the line 27}}{{sfnp|Özdemir|Özdemir|2021|p=272}}
<math display="block"> V = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{12}a^3 + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{12}a^3 + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^3 = \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \right) a^3 \approx 0.669a^3. </math>

[[File:3D Johnson J14.stl|thumb|3D model of an elongated triangular bipyramid]]
The elongated triangular bipyramid has the same [[Point groups in three dimensions|three-dimensional symmetry group]] as the triangular prism, the [[prismatic symmetry|three-fold prismatic symmetry]] <math> D_{3 \mathrm{h}} </math> of order twelve. It has an axis of threefold [[rotational symmetry]] (0°, 120°, 240°) through the apexes of the pyramids, three planes of mirror symmetry containing that axis, and a fourth plane of mirror symmetry perpendicular to that axis and passing through the solid's centroid.{{sfnp|Johnson|1966|loc=See "Table III: Non-Uniform Convex Polyhedra with Regular Faces" at the line 14}}{{sfnp|Özdemir|Özdemir|2021|p=272}}

The [[dihedral angle|dihedral angles]] of an elongated triangular bipyramid can be calculated by adding the angles of the tetrahedron and the triangular prism:{{sfnp|Johnson|1966|loc=See "Table III: Non-Uniform Convex Polyhedra with Regular Faces" at the line 14}}
* its dihedral angle between two adjacent triangular faces is that angle of a tetrahedron between two adjacent triangular faces: <math display="inline"> \arccos(\frac{1}{3}) \approx 70.5^\circ </math>;
* its dihedral angle between a square and a triangle is the sum of a triangular prism's square-to-triangle angle and a tetrahedron's triangle-to-triangle angle: <math display="inline"> \arccos(\frac{1}{3}) + \frac{\pi}{2} \approx 160.5^\circ </math>;
* the dihedral angle between two squares is that angle of a triangular prism's square-to-triangle, the [[internal angle]] of an equilateral triangle, <math display="inline"> \frac{\pi}{3} = 60^\circ </math>.

== Appearances ==
The nirrosula, an African musical instrument woven out of strips of plant leaves, is made in the form of a series of elongated bipyramids, although there are non-equilateral-triangular faces of their end caps.{{sfnp|Gerdes|2009|pp=13–14}}

The elongated triangular bipyramid, together with the [[helicoid]], is commonly found in the micromorphological structure of [[raphide|raphides]], needle-shape crystals made of [[calcium oxalate]] in [[plant]]s. These structures are specialized to regulate the [[product (biology)|product]]s of [[Metabolic activity|metabolic activities]] by transmitting, storing, and making them functionable, depending on the shapes.{{sfnp|Özdemir|Özdemir|2021|p=271}}
